## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 9, titled *Duṭṭhullārocana* ("Announcing a monk’s grave offense"), belongs to the Pācittiya chapter of the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates how monks handle and report the transgressions of fellow monastics [Hüsken 1997]: a monk who reveals another monk's serious offence (*duṭṭhulla*) to an unordained person incurs a *pācittiya* offence that must be confessed [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying case history is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
The rule corresponds to rule 9 in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and the Parivāra, and finds a counterpart for nuns in Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 105 [SuttaCentral]. Direct parallels are preserved across the Vinayas of other early Buddhist schools, including Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda recensions in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan, where it generally numbers among Pātayantika rules 7 to 9 [SuttaCentral; Clarke, Pārājika]. Automatic text-reuse calculations by DharmaNexus identify extensive shared material within the Pali canon, notably with the *Samuccayakkhandhaka* (Kd 13), Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiyas 47 and 64, and Vinaya commentaries (*Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā*), in addition to cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2) and Sanskrit *Pravāraṇāvastu* [DharmaNexus].
